traceability.notes:
The 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING story is fully implemented.
All acceptance criteria are satisfied: - Core Functionality & User Experience: Every core validation rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) defines clear, specific error messages via meta.messages, using placeholders like {{name}}, {{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, and {{storyPath}}. Tests assert both the templates and the data payloads, ensuring actionable guidance and contextual details. - Quality Standards & Integration: Messages are implemented using ESLint’s recommended pattern (meta.messages + messageId + data), and all rules integrate correctly with ESLint’s reporting and configuration system. Flat-config presets propagate the severities defined by TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES, verified by dedicated config tests. - Error Handling: The valid-story-reference and valid-req-reference rules distinguish between missing resources and filesystem/path errors, surfacing dedicated diagnostics like fileAccessError. At the plugin level, rule-loading failures are caught and transformed into clear ESLint diagnostics instead of hard failures, with corresponding tests. - Error Location & Context: Function-related rules provide functionName/name in data; file-related rules provide path/storyPath (and reqId for requirement lookups). ESLint’s normal location info (file, line, column) combines with these for precise localization, and the tests verify the data wiring. - Suggestions: require-story-annotation exposes hasSuggestions, fixable: 'code', and suggestion descriptors with prescriptive text and fix functions. error-reporting.test.ts explicitly validates the suggestion description and fix presence, satisfying REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION. - Documentation: This story file itself documents the cross-rule message conventions, and the rule/message JSDoc annotations reference this story and its REQ-ERROR-* IDs, providing traceable documentation of the conventions.
Given the up-to-date story file, the concrete rule implementations, and the passing, story-specific test suite, this story is correctly and completely implemented.
